# M00 motion, overlays and Group feasibility evidence

Scratch only. Production source, dependencies and generated styles were not edited.

Run with Bun 1.4.0 and the existing Playwright 1.63.0 cache:

```sh
PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=/var/folders/b6/2r9mrtsj70s3x013xbhxt2yr0000gn/T/acme-style-engines-fHTyxk/browsers bun run.ts
```

`fixture.ts` is the final compiled input. Rebuild with Bun.build({entrypoints:[fixture],outdir:build,target:'browser'}). `prepare.ts` and fix/extend scripts are historical, not an idempotent final build command. `run.ts` is the final runner. `results.json` is the final three-engine result. The old files preserve earlier fixture/integration failures; those results are not the final matrix.

## Outcome

Each engine: 24 passing candidate assertions and 3 expected red reproductions. Chromium 153.0.8010.48, Firefox 155.0, WebKit 26.6. No browser page errors. Reproductions are explicitly pass:false in the raw result because the same desired condition fails for the original code/reference pattern. They are not unexplained final test failures.

1. Current Interaction retains a window pointer listener and data-active when disconnected during a press. Candidate tracks the pointer/window lifetime, removes the listeners, and clears transient attributes. The window comes from the element's ownerDocument.
2. Current Overlay leaves body overflow:hidden after removing an open modal. Candidate native dialog lifetime keeps modality and body lock during its owned Lit Motion exit, cancels exit on reopen, releases immediately on removal, and ignores an unrelated infinite child animation. Same-task close/reopen and removal before queued animation starts pass.
3. Inline separators used as flex items become orphan dividers when wrapping at width150. Candidate uses the native flex gap for the required total separation and positions decorative dividers between measured same-line neighbors. Width150/220/350, row RTL, row-reverse, column/column-reverse, resize, hide and DOM reordering pass. Native child identity, focus and click handlers remain.
4. Actual Lit Motion animation moves/resizes the internal indicator in both axes. At 50 percent progress, its painted rectangle lies between the measured start/end rectangles; after completion it matches the selected target. Interruption begins from the current painted geometry with under1px change. Changed target size, reduced motion, selected-target removal and indicator removal pass.
5. Attached Group prototype has a real host box, padded outer outline and two actual shadow-contained native button surfaces. 1px and3px child borders overlap by the measured minimum1px, producing a single seam. Both orientations and RTL pass; the focused native button retains its2px outline and raised host stacking. This is representative feasibility, not visual approval of every Group appearance.

## Integration findings

Use one stable TanStack atom per instance; the getAtom callback returns that atom. An early fixture incorrectly created an atom in the callback; that fixture bug is preserved separately and fixed in the final input.

Ignore unchanged ResizeObserver geometry before cancelling motion. Capture the current painted rectangle before cancellation and use it for the next Lit Motion measurement. Queue the derived-geometry update in a microtask so the cancelled directive's completion bookkeeping settles before the next measurement; this removed the observed WebKit interruption failure. Semantic selection remains outside the indicator.

Use resting styles/native closed state rather than fill:both to retain an ended overlay animation. With fill:both, finished animations survived the controller's active-client cancellation in Firefox/WebKit. Final overlay uses fill:none and retains native modal ownership until the owned completion callback.

The modal candidate uses installed @zag-js/remove-scroll, Lit Motion1.1.0, Lit3.3.3 and the patched TanStack Lit Store0.13.2. The indicator and layout fixtures use the same Lit/Store runtime. CSS is scratch fixture CSS, not a production generator replacement.

## Bounds

This is M00 representative technical feasibility, not completed component acceptance. It does not certify Material spring-role mapping, final animation duration/easing, actual screenshot parity, nested overlay coordination, anchored Floating UI stale-placement behavior, cross-document overlay adoption, interactive outside-dismissal policies or screen-reader output. The 400ms linear duration exists only to inspect deterministic intermediate frames.

Stack's candidate uses measured cross-axis line starts for the tested aligned items. It does not yet establish unequal cross-axis alignment, wrap-reverse, vertical writing modes, CSS order, zero-size members or font-loading behavior. Those remain implementation acceptance cases; do not copy the limited line grouping verbatim as a complete final algorithm.

Group proof covers two documented button-like participating surfaces and padded outline. It does not establish coincident outer-perimeter suppression, mixed participant runs, dynamic defaults, nested groups, card selection/invalid state, input add-on labels/forms or forced colors. Those remain final implementation acceptance. No selection state is introduced into Group.

# M00 package-delivery fixture

Scratch only. No production files or repository dependencies changed. Bun 1.4.0.

The core tarball copies the existing Button, Spinner, base and three shared helpers/styles. Only registration placement/import extensions change. Existing TanStack atomState and its exact project lit-store patch are reused. This tests packaging, not the final rebuilt Button API. The separate React tarball uses @lit/react 1.0.8 and React 19.3.0 around the same class. It does not contain a second component implementation.

## Evidence

- verification.json: 152 passing assertions; browser outcomes and retained-module checks.
- browser-results.json: Chromium 153.0.8010.48, Firefox 155, WebKit 26.6; all 21 cases have no page errors or failed module/style requests.
- build-results.json: full consumer/CDN metafiles and sizes.
- baseline.json and baseline-named.json: current source delivery red cases; direct module registers Button and Spinner; named Button through root retains Chart/Table and 497 modules.
- workspace-pack/ and workspace-pack-exact/: Bun packs workspace:^ as ^0.0.1 and workspace:* as 0.0.1. Workspace install must precede pack; missing resolution fails loudly.
- consumer/bun.lock: exact tested dependency graph. Runtime implementation roots are unique in every retained graph. The lit umbrella re-export has no retained bytes; its resolution root is checked through metafile inputs.

## Reproduce

1. `bun registry.ts` starts a loopback-only registry and writes registry-url.txt. It serves the checked-in scratch tarballs and manifests with integrity, never publishes.
2. Set consumer/.npmrc to `@acmelabs:registry=<registry-url.txt>`, then `bun install --ignore-scripts --cwd consumer`. If reproducing with a new registry port, refresh the local fixture lock for that new registry; no user registry/auth configuration is touched.
3. `bun build.ts` builds the packed consumer fixtures and selective CDN entries with shared chunks. `bun baseline-named.ts` builds the current named Button root-import case.
4. `bun run.ts` executes all seven browser fixtures in each engine using the cached Playwright/browser paths recorded in that script.
5. `bun verify.ts` exits nonzero on a failed oracle and writes verification.json.

setup.ts and more.ts retain the initial source-copy and registration-split derivation. The final packed fixture additionally includes the real repository tokens.css and scoped native-document CSS. The first packaging attempt omitted tokens in the CDN test; its default Button background was transparent. The final fixture loads the packed token stylesheet and checks the expected nontransparent loading background. The custom-color tests alone would not have detected that omission.

A local-tarball-only install with an exact peer tried the public registry for the unpublished fixture core under Bun 1.4.0. Normal matching-version resolution succeeds through the isolated registry; this tests the actual registry delivery contract rather than certifying local-tarball peer installation.

## Boundaries

This closes representative M00 package feasibility, not the final package acceptance. Tests cover class-only no-registration import; HTML/Lit/React actual mount, object-property identity, native children, click mapping, scoped document CSS; React unmount; separate CDN entries with a transitive Spinner; token loading; no duplicate retained Lit/TanStack implementations; no charts/markdown/Solid/ELK/devtools; no debug map files or inline maps. It does not certify every final family, final CEM/types/exports, all style-order props, cross-version package coexistence, network/CDN cache behavior, public package publication, React SSR, or source-map debugger delivery. The fixture uses current Button shapes only as packaging content; no old API is endorsed for migration.
